meta.title: VBA to Office Scripts Migration | Sāra 0005 | TriSaar Consulting
meta.description: Sāra 0005 case study: migrating Excel report-generation automation from desktop-locked VBA macros to TypeScript-based Office Scripts for an asset management firm, enabling cross-platform execution on web, mobile and desktop, live SharePoint collaboration, and Power Automate orchestration.
meta.author: TriSaar Consulting

data.text: Modernizing Excel automation from desktop-locked VBA macros to cross-platform Office Scripts that run on web, mobile and desktop - with live SharePoint collaboration and Power Automate orchestration.

A migration initiative that replaced legacy VBA macros with TypeScript-based Office Scripts, enabling report automation across web, mobile and desktop while keeping the Excel workbook live and shared on SharePoint.

data.title: From desktop-locked macros to cross-platform automation.
data.subtitle: We migrated the client's VBA-driven Excel reporting to TypeScript-based Office Scripts, enabling the same automation to run on web, mobile and desktop while keeping workbooks live on SharePoint and orchestrated through Power Automate.

pillars.title: Excel automation was locked to the desktop.

As the team adopted browser-based and mobile Excel, the macros became unusable, files were emailed back and forth, and macro security warnings created friction for end users.

data.title: Excel automation was locked to the desktop - and the desktop was becoming the bottleneck.
data.body: The client's reporting workflow relied on VBA macros embedded in Excel workbooks to generate and format periodic reports. While the macros functioned reliably on desktop Excel, they could not run in Excel on the web or on mobile devices. As the team increasingly worked from browsers and phones, the macros became unusable, workbooks were emailed back and forth creating version conflicts, and macro-enabled files triggered security warnings that blocked adoption.

core.label: The Core Challenge
core.body: The automation was functional but locked to a single platform. As the team moved toward web and mobile Excel, VBA could not follow - and the desktop-only constraint was becoming an operational bottleneck.

points.title: Desktop-only execution
points.body: VBA macros only run in the desktop version of Excel. Team members working in browser-based or mobile Excel could not trigger the automation at all.

points.title: No live collaboration
points.body: Workbooks were emailed between team members rather than shared, leading to conflicting versions and no single source of truth for the latest report.

points.title: Security friction
points.body: Macro-enabled workbooks (.xlsm) triggered security warnings and IT restrictions, making it harder for end users to open and trust the files.

points.title: Legacy maintenance burden
points.body: VBA code was harder to maintain, debug and version-control. Smaller tasks that could benefit from automation were discouraged by the overhead of writing and distributing new macros.

impact.label: The Business Impact
impact.body: Report generation depended on who had the desktop file, when they were online, and whether macros were enabled. The workflow was functional but fragile, and the team could not take advantage of web, mobile or SharePoint collaboration.

data.title: A cross-platform migration from VBA to Office Scripts.
data.intro: We audited the client's existing VBA macros, rewrote their logic in TypeScript-based Office Scripts, and hosted the workbooks on SharePoint so they remained live and shared. Power Automate was integrated to trigger scripts on a schedule, enabling hands-free report generation without anyone needing to open Excel manually.

hub.label: Our Approach
hub.body: Modernize the automation layer without disrupting the familiar Excel workflow - replace the macro engine, not the spreadsheet.

steps.title: Audit VBA macros & document logic
steps.body: Catalogued every macro, its inputs, outputs, dependencies and formatting rules so the migration could be planned with no logic lost in translation.

steps.title: Rewrite in Office Scripts (TypeScript)
steps.body: Translated the VBA logic into TypeScript-based Office Scripts, leveraging the modern typed language for safer, more maintainable code that runs across all Excel surfaces.

steps.title: Host on SharePoint & enable sharing
steps.body: Moved the workbooks to SharePoint so the Excel file stayed live, shared and version-controlled. Multiple users could view and interact with the same file without emailing copies.

steps.title: Integrate Power Automate for scheduling
steps.body: Connected the Office Scripts to Power Automate flows so report generation could run on a schedule or be triggered by events - no manual intervention required.

items.title: Cross-platform execution
items.body: Scripts run on Excel for web, mobile and desktop - the same automation works everywhere.

items.title: Live SharePoint collaboration
